project_overview: This application appears to be a student information system, likely managing admissions, course selections, exam results, and student profiles. The codebase demonstrates a layered architecture, with components responsible for specific features and data management. The presence of several Vue components suggests a front-end focused user experience.  There is a notable reliance on services to handle core application logic.

layers.description: Contains core application logic and rules.

macro_trends.title: High-Level View Import
macro_trends.description: Multiple Vue components directly import services (e.g., `iLikeCourses.vue` importing `SelectedApplicationService.vue`). This indicates a potential lack of encapsulation and could lead to cascading changes if the service logic evolves. It suggests a need for a more robust abstraction layer.

macro_trends.title: State Management Fragility
macro_trends.description: The deeply nested component structure and frequent use of props suggests potential fragility in state management.  Changes in one component could inadvertently propagate through the component tree, causing unexpected behavior and difficult debugging.

key_workflows.name: Admission Workflow
key_workflows.description: The flow of data and logic related to student admissions, including application submission, processing, and confirmation.  This workflow involves several components, raising concerns about consistency and potential errors if not carefully managed.

key_workflows.name: Course Selection Workflow
key_workflows.description: The process of students selecting courses, which is reflected in multiple Vue components (e.g., `iLikeCourses.vue`). This workflow needs clear rules and validation to prevent conflicts.
